question: Does a rule that takes only the fills keeping two orders (never nesting), and subdivides otherwise, grow two-way grids without end from a line, with knots only on pairs that already share one (NN), at any cost (NN2), with any pairs (NNF), or by corners across crossing splits (CC)?

definitions.subdivision: one knot B(u, p, v) on an old pair differing on exactly one split
definitions.full grid: (a+1)(b+1) = n with a complete bipartite crossing graph
definitions.fill fraction: fills per step on steps 21 to 40

forbidden_inputs: Changing rules, starts, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: Predictions P1-P8 and the decision rule of research/NEVER-NEST-20261118-001/preregistration.md.
cheapest_meaningful_control: SUB (subdivisions only: two orders never formed, no fills) and KF3 (no two-order filter).

predictions.P1: NN intermediate at every start size
predictions.P2: NN passes a full grid at some n <= 40 in >= half the runs per start size, fewer from 8 than from 5
predictions.P3: NN median fill fraction, steps 21-40, in [0.25, 0.65] per start size
predictions.P4: NN no fill in steps 31-40 in <= 15% of runs per start size
predictions.P5: NN2 median fill fraction, steps 21-40, below NN's per start size
predictions.P6: KF3 two orders at n = 40 in <= 10% of runs per start size
predictions.P7: NNF (2x2 and every line) and CC (2x2): two orders at every step after the first, a full grid after every completed row or column, every run (proved; a check)
predictions.P8: CC after one fill of a line: a full grid at some n in < half the runs per start size

decision_rules.grows: median fill fraction >= 0.7, full grid at some n in 30-40 in >= 80% of runs, both chains growing after n = 20 in >= 80%
decision_rules.starved: median fill fraction <= 0.15, or no fill in steps 31-40 in >= 50% of runs
decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as stated in the pre-registration

runtime: E1 and E2 about 15 minutes, R1 about an hour on 12 processes, R2 about 5 minutes.
